text:
Alex DeBrincat was sixth of 401 forwards in Evolving-Hockey's wins above replacement last season, after 41 goals, and this year he has been Detroit's best skater most nights. With Dylan Larkin suspended, he's moved onto the top line beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, and the Wings hold 56% of the expected goals with him on.

Right now, though, he's cold: pointless in four, and unlike Arvidsson, the chances have thinned out too. He has five points in his last ten games against nine expected. That's what a team losing four straight looks like from the top line.

The skill is in the details. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot, and when his goals come they've counted: by our win probability, 15th in the league in wins added. Our range: 29 to 46 goals.
